newsitem.title: USA: U.S. March industrial output rose 0.9 pct.
newsitem.headline: U.S. March industrial output rose 0.9 pct.

text.p: Federal Reserve Board report of U.S. industrial production and capacity utilization, seasonally adjusted.
Total Industrial: Mar Feb Jan Dec Mar97/96
Percent of Capacity: Manufacturing, Mining, Utilities:
(Seasonally Adj.) Mar Feb Jan Dec Mar'96
Percent of Capacity: Manufacturing, Mining, Utilities:
(Seasonally Adj.) Mar Feb Jan Dec Mar'96

The increases in industrial output and in capacity use rates exceeded forecasts by Wall Street economists who had expected March production to rise 0.6 percent and estimated that March capacity use would be at a 83.6 percent rate.

The 0.9 percent increase in March industrial output was the largest since a matching 0.9 percent gain in April 1996. The 84.1 percent capacity use rate was the highest in two years, since an 84.3 percent rate in March 1995.

The Fed said that during the first quarter this year total industrial output had risen by 5.6 percent, up from a 4.5 percent increase in the fourth quarter of last year when growth was restrained by strikes in the auto industry.

The Fed said that most of the gains in industrial production during recent months have been in durable manufacturing. Overall manufacturing output increased by 0.9 percent in each of February and March.
Motor vehicle assemblies rose in March to a rate of 6.2 million a year for cars from 6.1 million in February. For light trucks the assembly rate was unchanged in March at 6.0 million.
Excluding motor vehicles and parts, March industrial output rose 0.8 percent after a 0.6 percent increase in February.
